title: Accompanying Ma Rainey and touring vaudeville shows at the Belmont
summary: She played piano for touring vaudeville and Ma Rainey, took her key at rehearsal; Jay McCobbs introduced.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I think we'll wait until we get, we'll try to get it in order. Okay. But I did want to ask you about, at that, were you living, did you, you played, did you, I don't think you said you played with these people, but I think you might have, do you
Mary Mack? Yeah. Billy and Mary Mack?

Yeah. Did you play with that show? Yeah. They used to come to Pensacola. You see what they used to do, all of them there, vaudeville people, you know, shows, they used to come through Pensacola, and they always would stop at the Belmont Theater. And sometimes they'd have their own piano piano piano, and sometimes they didn't. So they always got the good to one of the good to one of the girls. So I would have to be one of them, at the time some of them, and then sometimes it'd get my sister Billy, Ida, and Edna, either one of them, that you could play for. And Bester Snipp comes through there, Bester Snipp and all that. Now I played with Mom Rainey, and I played for her vaudeville, and I played for, they had a vaudeville with the Barn Bailey show. Barn Bailey, the circus?
So they needed the piano player. So I went that time to go there then, I played the piano there for that Barn Bailey circus show. They didn't have a band with them?
No, no, they didn't have a band with them. My Rainey didn't? She never traveled with a band with them?
No, no, no, she didn't either, no. Just piano player they get. That's all? That's all they would have in Pensacola. Just get a piano player.
Would they give you the music to play, or?
Well, no, what we do, we go to rehearsal, and they tell you what song they want you to play. And then they'd give me the key, the key they sing it in. So that's what we used to do.
Yeah. Did she sing in different keys, My Rainey?
Well, she used to mostly sing, mostly all of her keys she's singing mostly was B-flat.
What if you wouldn't know a song that she wanted to do?
Well then you'd rehearse it all over with her.
She was pretty good to work with her?

Oh yeah, she was good to work with her. She was good to work with her. In fact, every one of them that I ever played with her on the vaudeville, she was, you know, good to work with her. Now this white fella that owned this theater, he probably raised my mother. Jay McCobbs his name was. White guy.
